subject: Computer Studies
examFormat: Three papers, all of which must be taken; Papers 1 and 2 form a composite paper taken at one sitting. Paper 1: 50 multiple-choice objective questions, all to be answered in 1 hour for 25 marks. Paper 2: five essay questions, any three to be answered in 1 hour for 30 marks. Paper 3: tests actual practical skills of school candidates and knowledge of practical work for private candidates; three questions to be answered in 2 hours for 45 marks.

topics.name: Computer Evolution
topics.content: Computing devices I (pre-computing age to 19th century) and II (20th century to date). The trend of development in computing devices from one to the other is considered; sizes and basic components are treated in a comparative form.

subtopics.name: Computing Devices I (Pre-computing Age to 19th Century)
objectives: Describe the features, components and uses of early computing devices: abacus, slide rule, Napier's bones, Pascal's calculator, Leibnitz multiplier, Jacquard loom, Charles Babbage's analytical engine, Hollerith census machine and Burroughs' machine
Explain the contribution of the founder of each of these devices to modern computers

subtopics.name: Computing Devices II (20th Century to Date)
objectives: Describe the features, components and uses of ENIAC, EDVAC, UNIVAC 1, desktop personal computers, laptop and notebook computers, and palmtops

topics.name: Fundamentals of Computing
topics.content: Differences between hardware and software should be treated.

subtopics.name: Overview of Computing System
objectives: Define a computer
State the two main constituents of a computer: hardware and software
Classify hardware and software and give examples
Identify the functional parts of a computer
State the characteristics of computers: electronic in nature, accuracy, speed, interactive, etc.

subtopics.name: Data and Information
objectives: Define data and information and give examples
Distinguish between data and information

topics.name: Computer Ethics and Human Issues
topics.content: Definition and effects of viruses and worms, definitions of hackers and spammers, and explanations of firewall and encryption should be treated.

subtopics.name: Sources of Security Breaches
objectives: Identify the sources of security breaches: viruses, worms and Trojan horses; poor implementation of networks; poor implementation or lack of ICT policies; carelessness in giving out personal and vital information on the net; hackers, spammers, etc.

subtopics.name: Preventive Measures
objectives: Describe preventive measures: use of antivirus software (e.g. Norton, McAfee, Avast), firewalls, care in giving out personal information, encryption, proper network implementation and policies, use of sites with web certificates, and care in opening e-mail attachments

subtopics.name: Legal Issues
objectives: Explain software copyright and ownership rights to text, images, audio and video
Explain the privacy of audio and video software
Identify cyber crimes: identity theft, internet fraud and hacking

subtopics.name: Input Devices
objectives: Define input devices and give examples
Describe the use of the keyboard, mouse, scanner, joystick, light pen, etc.
Classify keyboard keys into function, numeric, alphabetic and cursor keys
Describe the features, function and operation of the mouse
State the differences between the keyboard, mouse, light pen and scanner

subtopics.name: Output Devices
objectives: Define output devices and give examples
Describe the type, features and uses of the monitor, printer, speaker and plotter
Distinguish between input and output devices
State the similarities and differences between inkjet, laser and line printers

subtopics.name: Central Processing Unit
objectives: Identify the components of the CPU: arithmetic and logic unit and control unit
State the functions of the ALU and the control unit

subtopics.name: Memory Unit
objectives: Distinguish between primary and secondary memory
Identify the components of primary memory: ROM and RAM, and state their differences and uses
Give examples of secondary memory devices: floppy disk, hard disk, compact disk, flash disk and digital video disk
State the units of storage: bits, nibble, bytes, kilobytes, megabytes, gigabytes and terabytes, and convert between them
Compare auxiliary storage devices in respect of size, speed and technology

subtopics.name: Logic Circuits
objectives: Define the standard logic gates AND, NOT and OR, state their types and uses and draw their symbols
Construct truth tables for the standard logic gates and state their logic equations
Treat NAND and NOR as alternative logic gates and construct their truth tables
Construct a simple comparator with XOR and NOR gates

topics.name: Computer Software
topics.content: Operating systems of phones, iPads and other computerized devices (e.g. Android, Blackberry) should be treated. Differences between system and application software, among translators, and between GUI and command line operating systems are required.

subtopics.name: System Software
objectives: Define and state the types of software: system software and application software
Identify system software and give examples: operating system (e.g. MS Windows), translator (e.g. compiler), tools/utility (e.g. anti-virus)
Give examples of operating systems: MS Windows, Linux, UNIX, MS-DOS, etc.
Give examples of translators: assemblers, compilers and interpreters
Give examples of utility programs: editor, anti-virus, etc.

subtopics.name: Operating System
objectives: Define an operating system and state its types, examples and functions
Distinguish between graphic user interface (e.g. MS Windows, Linux) and command line (e.g. MS-DOS, UNIX) operating systems

subtopics.name: Application Software
objectives: Define and state the types of application software
Identify common application packages and give examples: word processing (MS Word), spreadsheet (MS Excel), database (MS Access), graphics
Identify other packages: accounting, payroll, banking, education management, statistical and hospital management software
Distinguish between user application programs and application packages

subtopics.name: Word Processing
objectives: Define word processing and word processor and give examples: MS Word, Wordstar, WordPerfect
State the features of word processing programs and of MS Word in general
State the application areas of word processing: office, publishing, journalism, education, etc.
Activate and exit MS Word
Carry out basic operations in MS Word: create, edit, save, retrieve, print and close
Carry out further operations: move, copy, cut, use different types and sizes of fonts, formatting, justifying, search/explore, spell checking, file merging, etc.

subtopics.name: Spreadsheet
objectives: Define a spreadsheet and give examples: VisiCalc, MS Excel, SuperCalc, etc.
State the features of spreadsheet programs and their application areas: accounting, statistical calculation, student results, etc.
Identify features of the MS Excel environment: status bar, menu bar, formula bar, etc.
Define worksheet, workbook, cells and cell ranges
Identify data types in Excel: number, labels and formula
Carry out basic operations in Excel: data entry, saving, retrieving, copying and moving
Perform arithmetic calculations using formulae and built-in functions (e.g. sum, average)
Carry out additional operations: editing, formatting, printing and drawing charts (pie chart, histogram, bar chart, etc.)

subtopics.name: Database
objectives: Define a database and database packages and give examples: dBase IV, Foxbase, MS Access, Oracle, etc.
Define the basic terms: file, record, field and key
Describe the types of database organization and their features: hierarchical, network and relational

State the features of database format: files designed as tables, tables comprising rows and columns, rows containing related information about a record, columns containing a specific type of information about a field
Describe the steps in creating a database: define the structure, indicate field types, enter data and save data
Carry out basic operations on an already created database: searching, modifying, sorting, reporting, selecting, inserting, etc.

subtopics.name: Graphics
objectives: Define graphics and give examples of graphics packages: Paint, Harvard Graphics, Photoshop, CorelDraw, etc.
Activate and exit CorelDraw
Produce simple designs using CorelDraw, e.g. business card, school logo, national flag, invitation card, certificate

subtopics.name: Presentation Package
objectives: Define a presentation package and give examples, e.g. MS PowerPoint
Identify the features of the PowerPoint environment
Activate and exit PowerPoint
Carry out PowerPoint operations: create a new presentation, insert pictures, text and graphs, add animated contents, add a new slide, save, run a slide show, print and close a presentation

topics.name: Managing Computer Files
topics.content: Differences among the file organization methods are required. File processing using BASIC programming is required.

subtopics.name: Concept of Computer Files
objectives: Define computer file, record, field and data item
Identify the types of data item: numeric, alphabetic and alphanumeric
Describe the file structure organization: data item, record, file, database
Describe the types of file organization: serial, sequential, index and random
Describe the methods of accessing files: serial, sequential and random
Classify files as master file, transaction file and reference file
State the criteria for classifying files: nature of content (program and data), organization method and storage medium

subtopics.name: Handling Computer Files
objectives: Carry out basic operations on computer files: file, delete, retrieve, insert, copy, view, update, open and close
Explain the effects of file insecurity: data loss, data corruption and data becoming unreliable
State the causes of data loss: over-writing and inadvertent deletion
Describe methods of file security: use of backup, antivirus, passwords and proper labelling of storage devices
Distinguish between computer files and manual files
State the advantages of computer files (more secure, fast to access, etc.) and disadvantages (expensive to set up, irregular supply of electricity)

topics.name: Basic Computer Operations
topics.content: The difference between cold and warm booting should be treated. The fetch-execute cycle is not required.

subtopics.name: Booting and Shutting Down Process
objectives: Describe booting and the types of booting process: cold booting and warm booting
Describe the steps involved in booting and shutting down a computer
Identify features on a desktop

subtopics.name: Computer Data Conversion
objectives: Define registers, address and bus
State the types and functions of registers: MDR, CIR, SCR
Distinguish between registers and main memory
Describe the steps involved in how a computer converts data to required information (Input-Process-Output)
Explain the factors affecting the speed of data transfer: bus speed and bus width

topics.name: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
topics.content: Definitions and descriptions of teleconferencing, video conferencing and telecommuting are required. Knowledge of the operations of ICT-based gadgets is required. Demonstration of Internet terms through Internet access is required. The benefits of the Internet to society should be stressed. The procedure for sending and receiving e-mail is required. Differences among network topologies should be treated; knowledge of the bridge as a networking device is required. Nigeria's contribution to the www, the use of HTTP and HTML, and software for web development (e.g. FrontPage) should be mentioned; visits to the listed websites are essential.

subtopics.name: Communication Systems
objectives: State what the acronym ICT stands for
Identify the types of ICT: broadcasting, telecommunication, data network, information systems and satellite communications

Give examples of broadcasting (radio, television, satellite system) and telecommunication (PSTN landline, mobile phone systems, circuit switched packet telephone system, satellite telephone system, fixed wireless telephone system)
Give examples of data networks (PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, Internet) and information systems (data processing system, GPS)

subtopics.name: Application Areas of ICT
objectives: Describe the application areas of ICT: teleconferencing, video conferencing and telecommuting
Describe ICT-based gadgets and their operations: mobile phones, computers, fax machines, ATMs, dispensing machines, point of sale machines, automated cash registers, radio sets, television sets, etc.

subtopics.name: Internet Access
objectives: Define the Internet and Internet terms: homepage, browse, browser, chatroom, cybercafe, HTTP, HTML, ISP, webpage, website, etc.
Identify types of Internet browsers: Internet Explorer, Netscape Navigator, Opera, Firefox, Cometbird, etc.
Identify features of Internet browsers: title bar, menu bar, tool bar, address bar, etc.
Identify types of Internet services: e-mail, e-mail discussion group, instant messaging, Telnet, Usenet, FTP, worldwide web and chatting

subtopics.name: Electronic Mail (E-mail) Services
objectives: Define electronic mail
Describe e-mail services: sending/receiving e-mail and chatting
Describe the steps in creating an e-mail account and in opening a mail box
Identify the features of an e-mail address
Define chatting and describe the steps involved

subtopics.name: Networking
objectives: Define a computer network
Identify the types of network: PAN, LAN, WAN, MAN and Internet
Describe network topologies: star, bus and ring
Identify network devices: hub, modems, switches, routers and network interface card (NIC)
State the advantages of networking

subtopics.name: Introduction to the Worldwide Web (W.W.W.)
objectives: State what the acronym W.W.W. stands for and give a brief history of the W.W.W.
Explain basic terminologies: W.W.W., website, webpage, homepage, protocol, etc.
Describe the protocols HTTP and HTML
State the uses and benefits of the www and navigate through websites
Distinguish between e-mail and website address features
Identify software for web development

subtopics.name: Cables and Connectors
objectives: Identify types of network cables (twisted pair, coaxial, fibre optic, telephone) and connectors (RJ45, RJ11, T-connectors)
Identify types of computer cables (power cables; data cables such as printer cable, USB, monitor cable and serial cable) and connectors (male and female)

topics.name: Developing Problem-Solving Skills
topics.content: Other programming languages such as Java and Python should be mentioned. The number of iterations should not exceed eight (8). A flow diagram of how a compiler and an interpreter work is required.

subtopics.name: Programming Language
objectives: Define a programming language and state its examples, levels and features
Identify the levels of programming language: machine language, low level language (e.g. assembly language) and high level language (e.g. BASIC, C++, FORTRAN)
Compare machine, low level and high level languages and state their advantages and disadvantages

subtopics.name: High Level Languages
objectives: Define high level languages and give examples
Classify high level languages as scientific, general-purpose, business, AI and string processing languages
Compare the features of BASIC, C, PASCAL and COBOL

subtopics.name: Algorithm and Flowchart
objectives: Define algorithm and flowchart and state the functions of an algorithm
State the characteristics of an algorithm: finite, effective and unambiguous
Write algorithms for computing the average of a given set of numbers, evaluating an equation such as y = a(b-c)^2/(d+2), and computing the first ten odd numbers
Identify flowchart symbols (I/O, process, decisions, etc.) and state the use of each
Draw flowchart diagrams for given programming problems

subtopics.name: BASIC Programming
objectives: State what the acronym BASIC stands for and its characteristics
Identify types of data: variable, constant/literal, numeric and string/alphanumeric
Use BASIC statements: INPUT, PRINT, LPRINT, LET, END, REM, READ and DATA
Use arithmetic operators and evaluate arithmetic expressions
Write and run simple BASIC programs (e.g. area of a triangle or rectangle, average of 3 numbers)
Use built-in functions in BASIC: SQR(X), INT(X), SIN(X), ABS(X), RND(X), COS(X), TAN(X), LOG(X) and EXP(X)
Write BASIC notation for expressions and write programs to find square roots, cosines and tangents and plot a sine wave curve
Use the DIM, FOR-NEXT and WHILE-END statements
Define one-dimensional arrays using DIM and operate on array elements (input, output and arithmetic operations)
Write BASIC programs to store a vector of 10 numbers, calculate the mean of 100 numeric values, calculate the area of 10 different rectangles and compute the sum of the first 100 integers

subtopics.name: Systems Development Cycle
objectives: Define and describe the system development cycle
State and describe the stages: preliminary study, feasibility, investigative study, analysis, design, implementation, maintenance and study review
Draw a diagram of the system development cycle

subtopics.name: Program Development Cycle
objectives: Define a program
State the characteristics of a good program: accuracy, readability, maintainability, efficiency, generality and clarity
State the precautions in developing a program: be stable, steady and patient; no step skipping; follow order of execution
Describe the steps in program development: problem definition, problem analysis, flow charting, desk checking, program coding, program compilation, program testing/debugging and program documentation
Give examples of interpreted (BASIC) and compiled (COBOL, FORTRAN) programs
